mission: Adversarial preflight audit of the Tier 3 architecture-vs-model design. No implementation, no execution, no fine-tuning, no production changes.

blockers.title: Confirmed real, previously-undisclosed token-budget asymmetry: PIPELINE gets 2048 tokens, RAW/COUNCIL (as actually executed) got 1024
blockers.evidence: Direct source read. echo_query() (called inside generate_code_from_plan(), the real Condition B/PIPELINE path) explicitly passes max_tokens=_TASK_TOKEN_LIMITS.get('coding', 1024) = 2048 to ollama_query(). The pilot script's Condition A call (_ollama_query(model_name, prompt, temperature=0.0, task_type='coding')) and Condition C call (deliberate_and_learn(prompt=..., task_type='coding', river_brain=proxy, model_pool=MODEL_POOL)) BOTH omit max_tokens entirely -- confirmed via source read of _ollama_query() and deliberate_and_learn()'s own default (max_tokens: Optional[int]=None), which propagates to stream_query_ollama()'s own bare default of 1024. This means the ALREADY-EXECUTED 22-candidate RAW/PIPELINE/COUNCIL pilot has PIPELINE running at 2x the token budget of RAW and COUNCIL, undisclosed in any prior report.
blockers.impact: Directly threatens the Tier 3 design's central Level-A isolation claim (ARCH_PIPELINE vs. BASE_1 'same single-call budget') -- a call-count match is not a token-budget match. It also retroactively means the prior pilot's own task_03/task_06 opposite-direction result cannot be cleanly attributed to condition identity without controlling for this.
blockers.classification: FATAL CONFOUND for the Level-A comparison as currently specified; not yet fatal for the H1-vs-H4 comparison (both arms there currently default to the SAME 1024, so they are at least symmetric with each other, though not matched to production's real 2048 ceiling).
blockers.minimum_repair: Explicitly pass max_tokens=2048 (the real _TASK_TOKEN_LIMITS['coding'] value) to every arm's every call -- BASE_1, BASE_N (each attempt AND the synthesis call), ARCH_PIPELINE, and ARCH_COUNCIL (both per-councillor and synthesis) -- a small, mechanical, one-line-per-call-site fix, not a redesign.

blockers.title: BASE_N_selfconsistency has zero implementation -- every claim about it is currently unverifiable prose
blockers.evidence: grep across the entire codebase and scripts/run_capability_pilot.py confirms no function, prompt, or call sequence implementing 'N attempts + same-model synthesis' exists anywhere. The design document describes it functionally but specifies neither its exact synthesis prompt, nor whether it reuses SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE, nor its per-attempt temperature policy precisely enough to code from without further decisions.
blockers.impact: The entire H1-vs-H4 discrimination this Tier 3 design exists to provide rests on an arm that does not yet exist in any runnable form. Every 'audit' of BASE_N's equivalence to ARCH_COUNCIL in this document is necessarily an audit of a PROPOSAL, not a verified implementation -- a materially different epistemic status than the other three arms, which were verified directly against real, already-executed code.
blockers.classification: BLOCKER -- not a flaw in the design's logic, but a real gap between 'designed' and 'implementable as designed' that must be closed with concrete decisions before any code is written.
blockers.minimum_repair: Before writing any code: (a) decide and document BASE_N's exact synthesis prompt (see B3, this cannot be deferred), (b) decide and document per-attempt temperature (a single fixed value, or jittered like council's real per-councillor jitter -- another currently-unspecified parity question), (c) decide whether BASE_N's N attempts are generated sequentially or how failures among them are handled (does a single failed attempt among N abort the whole arm, or is it dropped and synthesis proceeds with N-1? Council's own real deliberate_and_learn() has an explicit 'valid_opinions' filter for exactly this case -- BASE_N needs an equivalent, explicitly matched rule, not an implicit one).

blockers.title: The real council synthesis prompt (SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE) explicitly frames its input as 'a council has offered perspectives' and exposes real per-model identity labels ([1. Echo], [2. Qwen2], ...) -- BASE_N's synthesis prompt equivalence was never actually specified against this
blockers.evidence: Direct source read of river_deliberation.py: SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE's literal text says 'The council has offered the following perspectives...' and instructs the synthesizer to 'identify the sharpest point of tension... do not resolve tension artificially.' _format_opinions() labels each entry with the real model's short name (e.g. 'Qwen2', 'Deepseek-r1'), not an anonymous index.
blockers.impact: Two mutually exclusive, both-bad options if left unresolved: (1) reuse this exact template verbatim for BASE_N -- but it would be LITERALLY FALSE for a same-model self-consistency check ('the council has offered perspectives' when there is no council), and the instruction to find 'the sharpest tension' between N outputs from ONE model (which likely differ only stochastically, not in genuine viewpoint) could cause the model to manufacture or over-weight spurious disagreement, artificially degrading BASE_N's own true ceiling and INFLATING any apparent ARCH_COUNCIL advantage for a reason having nothing to do with real model diversity. (2) write a new, custom synthesis prompt for BASE_N -- but then the synthesis MECHANISM itself is no longer held constant across the comparison, introducing a fresh, undisclosed confound in exactly the place (§4's 'synthesis control') the design most needs equivalence.
blockers.classification: BLOCKER -- this is not a minor wording detail; it directly determines whether a BASE_N-vs-ARCH_COUNCIL result can be attributed to model diversity at all.
blockers.minimum_repair: Use a deliberately MINIMAL, honest edit of the real template: replace 'The council has offered the following perspectives' with 'You previously produced the following independent attempts', and replace named-model labels ([1. Qwen2]) with anonymous, parallel-structured labels ([Attempt 1], [Attempt 2]) for BOTH arms -- i.e., additionally strip real model identity from ARCH_COUNCIL's own synthesis input too, so the ONLY thing that differs between the two arms' synthesis calls is whether the underlying attempts actually came from different models, not whether the synthesis prompt ADMITS that they did. This is the single smallest change that closes the gap without inventing a new mechanism.

major_issues.title: Model diversity and council orchestration structure are conflated -- the 4-arm design cannot distinguish them
major_issues.detail: BASE_N is homogeneous (one model, N times); ARCH_COUNCIL is both heterogeneous (N different models) AND structured (real _select_council() ranking/tag-boost logic, a specific synthesis-instruction set). If ARCH_COUNCIL beats BASE_N, the legitimate conclusion is bounded: 'council's REAL, COMBINED package (diversity + selection + synthesis structure) beats a budget-matched single model' -- NOT 'model diversity specifically helps' and NOT 'architecture specifically helps', because the experiment cannot separate which of the two co-occurring differences (diversity vs. structure) drove the result.
major_issues.classification: MAJOR -- does not invalidate the experiment, but bounds its legitimate conclusion more narrowly than the design document's own language ('model diversity advantage... architecture advantage') implies.
major_issues.minimum_repair_not_required_but_noted: A fifth arm, DIVERSE_N (N different models, independent, combined via the SAME minimal non-oracle rule as BASE_N -- e.g. simple concatenation-then-single-model-pick, NOT the real council selection logic), would cleanly separate diversity from council-specific structure. NOT recommended for addition now -- the mission's own instruction is to determine whether the four-arm experiment can answer the intended question without it, and it can, at the cost of a narrower, more honestly-scoped claim (see 'final_claim_boundary').

major_issues.title: 'choose_model() pinned once per batch' is insufficient for a multi-day/multi-batch study
major_issues.detail: The design document says pinning happens 'at batch start.' Given this investigation's own demonstrated need for multiple controlled batches across real, separate invocations (proven necessary in the executed pilot), a fresh choose_model() call at the start of EVERY batch could select a DIFFERENT model between batches, silently reintroducing the exact uncontrolled-model-selection confound the pinning was meant to remove.
major_issues.minimum_repair: Pin once for the ENTIRE study (not per batch): persist the chosen model name to a small state file at the first invocation, and have every subsequent batch invocation read and reuse that persisted value rather than re-calling choose_model() -- the same persistence discipline the harness's own resumability logic already uses for candidate IDs.

major_issues.title: GENERATION_TRUNCATED does not exist in the actual harness code -- it is a design-document proposal only
major_issues.detail: The real script's exception/failure-classification logic currently has exactly two paths: a real objective_verify() failure becomes TASK_LOGIC_FAILURE unconditionally, and a raised exception becomes INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE or GENERATION_EXCEPTION via _classify_exception(). A truncated-mid-fence response (candidate_019's real, already-observed failure mode) currently WOULD be silently labeled TASK_LOGIC_FAILURE by the existing code, exactly the conflation the design document itself says it closes.
major_issues.classification: MAJOR -- the design's own §12 claims this gap is closed; it is not, in code, yet.
major_issues.minimum_repair: Add one check before the failure-class assignment: if the raw response contains an OPENING fence with no matching CLOSING fence, assign GENERATION_TRUNCATED instead of TASK_LOGIC_FAILURE -- a small, localized addition to the existing clean_code()/scoring logic, not a redesign.

major_issues.title: Arm execution order was not randomized in the actually-executed pilot, and Tier 3's design does not yet specify randomization either
major_issues.detail: The controlled continuation processed tasks in fixed suite order, A-then-B-then-C per task, not randomized -- confirmed by direct inspection of the real resumability logic (`for cond in ['A','B','C']`, a fixed loop, not shuffled). Given this investigation has independently, repeatedly measured REAL, rising swap pressure and real model-residency churn across the session, a fixed A-B-C order risks a systematic bias: whichever arm consistently runs last per task inherits whatever cache/swap/thermal state the earlier two arms left behind, a confound orthogonal to any arm's real merit.
major_issues.classification: MAJOR for Tier 3 specifically, since its comparisons are exactly the paired, task-matched ones most sensitive to a systematic per-task ordering bias.
major_issues.minimum_repair: Randomize arm order independently for each held-out task (not once for the whole study) -- a one-line change to however the task/condition pair list is constructed, not a new mechanism.

major_issues.title: 'Statistical indistinguishability... read as support for H4 over H1' is too strong, exactly as flagged for audit
major_issues.detail: At n=8 held-out tasks, a non-significant McNemar's result is the EXPECTED outcome whether the true effect is zero OR whether it is real but the study is simply underpowered to detect it at this n -- these two states are not distinguishable from a p-value alone. The design's own go/no-go criteria list BOTH 'NO_GO_on_H1_supports_H4' (triggered by indistinguishability) AND 'AMBIGUOUS' (triggered by insufficient power) without a rule for which applies when the SAME empirical result (a small, non-significant pilot) could trigger either label.
major_issues.classification: MAJOR -- a real internal inconsistency in the design's own interpretation rules, not merely an abstract statistical nitpick.
major_issues.minimum_repair: Add an explicit disambiguating rule using the OBSERVED point-estimate effect size, not just the p-value: if the observed pass-rate difference is small (e.g. <=10pp) with a reasonably tight confidence interval, read as genuine support for H4/null; if the observed difference is large (e.g. >=15-20pp) but the confidence interval is wide and crosses zero, read as AMBIGUOUS/underpowered, NOT as support for H4 -- a one-paragraph addition to the existing interpretation rules, not a new statistical framework.

major_issues.title: F1, as actually wired in the harness, cannot affect scoring at all -- the F1 correctness prediction is trivially, structurally true rather than a genuine empirical test
major_issues.detail: Direct source read of run_condition_b_pipeline(): F1's verdict (f1_passed/f1_detail) is recorded but the candidate proceeds to objective_verify() unconditionally regardless of F1's result -- there is no code path where F1 rejects a candidate, triggers regeneration, or alters what gets scored. Combined with F1's own real implementation (a pure AST safety-call blocklist scan with zero semantic/execution analysis, confirmed by direct source read of scan_for_unsafe_operations()), F1 CANNOT affect PASS/FAIL by construction, in this harness, today -- not merely 'expected to contribute near zero.'
major_issues.classification: MAJOR, but favorably resolved -- this makes the F1 prediction TRIVIALLY true rather than falsified, which is itself worth stating plainly rather than presenting as a meaningful empirical test: as currently wired, no observed result could ever falsify 'F1 contributes zero to correctness', because the code structurally guarantees it.
major_issues.minimum_repair: Either (a) explicitly relabel this as a structural fact verified by code inspection, not an experimental finding Tier 3 will 'discover', or (b) if a genuine empirical test of F1's correctness-relevance is wanted, wire F1 to actually gate the candidate (reject and mark FAIL on any F1 violation) as a clearly-labeled fifth micro-check -- not recommended as part of the core 4-arm design, since (a) is cheaper and the prediction's truth is already established by direct code inspection, which is stronger evidence than an experimental result would be for a purely structural claim.

minor_issues.title: Multiple comparisons (2 paired tests: COUNCIL-vs-BASE_N, PIPELINE-vs-BASE_1)
minor_issues.repair: note a Bonferroni-adjusted alpha (0.025) alongside the primary 0.05 threshold when reporting; the pre-specified 25-30pp effect size already provides a large safety margin against this being decisive either way

minor_issues.title: Held-out tasks are written by the same investigator who has seen 22 real pilot failures
minor_issues.classification: ACCEPTABLE, stated explicitly not glossed over
minor_issues.repair: none required -- this is 'held out from mechanism tuning' (genuinely true: no arm's code/prompts were adjusted based on any task-level result) but NOT 'held out from investigator prior knowledge of general LLM failure modes' (an unrealistic standard requiring a blind third party); the distinction should be stated in the final report, not silently assumed away

minor_issues.title: Development-set tasks (task_11, task_12) are themselves drawn from real historical self-edit failure shapes, same as the held-out set's intended category spread
minor_issues.repair: none required -- using development tasks only to sanity-check non-degeneracy, never to tune, is the correct mitigation and is already specified

minor_issues.title: Independent 20% spot-check may itself be under-powered to catch a rare, systematic evaluator bias affecting only one arm
minor_issues.repair: stratify the spot-check to guarantee at least 1-2 candidates per arm are manually reviewed, not a pure random 20% that could by chance skip an entire arm at n=32

ARCH_COUNCIL.temperature: per-councillor JITTERED (real production behavior, confirmed via source, not fixed 0.0) -- a disclosed, intentional asymmetry vs. BASE_1/ARCH_PIPELINE's temp=0.0

ARCH_COUNCIL.synthesis_mechanism: SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE, confirmed to expose real per-model identity labels and 'council of perspectives' framing (see B3)

budget_audit.calls_matched: yes, by design, between BASE_N and ARCH_COUNCIL (N+1 each) once BASE_N is built; BASE_1 and ARCH_PIPELINE both use exactly 1 call
budget_audit.tokens_matched: NO -- confirmed real asymmetry, see B1. Call-count parity does not imply token-budget parity, exactly the trap the mission's own Section 7 named in advance.
budget_audit.prompt_content_matched: NO, and not intended to be for the Level-A test specifically -- ARCH_PIPELINE's prompt is confirmed larger (includes the full current self_edit_generated.py file) than BASE_1's bare task text; this IS the manipulated variable for that specific comparison, not a confound, PROVIDED token budget is also fixed (see B1) so the comparison isolates framing, not framing-plus-more-room-to-use-it.
budget_audit.model_parameter_count_matched: NOT ENFORCED -- ARCH_COUNCIL's real model selection draws from a 9-model pool of varying sizes (3B-8B class); BASE_N/BASE_1/ARCH_PIPELINE use one pinned model. This is an intentional, disclosed asymmetry for the diversity-vs-compute question, not an oversight, but should be stated as such rather than silently assumed 'equal'.
budget_audit.wall_clock_not_used_as_the_budget_defini: correctly so -- wall-clock varies with real, uncontrolled infrastructure contention (already demonstrated extensively this investigation) and would itself be a confounded proxy for compute; call-count + token-budget together is the more defensible operational definition, once B1 is fixed
budget_audit.operational_definition_recommended: equal number of real model calls AND equal max_tokens per call, held identical across all four arms -- NOT wall-clock, NOT a vague notion of 'similar effort'

synthesis_equivalence.candidate_count: matched by design (N for both, once BASE_N exists)
synthesis_equivalence.candidate_content_available: matched in principle, NOT yet matched in practice (B3 -- model-identity labels differ)
synthesis_equivalence.metadata_available: CONFIRMED DIFFERENT -- council exposes real model names; BASE_N's design never specified whether it would (repair: strip from both, see B3)
synthesis_equivalence.system_instructions: CONFIRMED DIFFERENT as currently specified (BASE_N has no written prompt at all yet; council's real template's 'council of perspectives' framing would be false if reused verbatim -- see B3)
synthesis_equivalence.token_budget: CONFIRMED CURRENTLY UNMATCHED to production reality for either arm's synthesis call (both default to 1024, see B1) and UNSPECIFIED for BASE_N's design
synthesis_equivalence.selection_criteria: council's real template explicitly instructs weighing coherence/relevance and surfacing genuine tension -- BASE_N's equivalent instruction was never written (part of B3's repair)
synthesis_equivalence.ability_to_reject_all_candidates: council's real deliberate_and_learn() has explicit fallback paths for all-councillors-errored; BASE_N's equivalent handling was never specified (part of B2's repair)

classification_per_item.temperature_policy: REQUIRED_DIFFERENCE if BASE_N uses jittered temp per attempt (mirrors council's real jitter) -- ACCEPTABLE once explicitly decided and documented, currently UNDECIDED

model_diversity_analysis.reasoning: see major_issues M1 -- BASE_N (homogeneous) vs ARCH_COUNCIL (heterogeneous + structured) confounds two co-occurring differences. A win for ARCH_COUNCIL cannot be attributed to diversity alone or to orchestration-structure alone from this comparison.
model_diversity_analysis.minimum_additional_control_for_full_sepa: a fifth arm, DIVERSE_N: N different models (same real _select_council() pool/choice), combined via the SAME minimal, non-oracle rule as BASE_N (not council's real structured synthesis) -- this would isolate diversity (DIVERSE_N vs BASE_N) from orchestration-structure (ARCH_COUNCIL vs DIVERSE_N) as two separate, cleanly interpretable deltas.
model_diversity_analysis.recommendation: do NOT add this arm now -- the mission's own instruction is to determine whether the existing four-arm design can answer the intended question without it. It can, at a narrower scope: the defensible claim is bounded to 'council's real, combined package vs. a single model at equal budget', not a decomposed diversity-vs-structure claim. This narrower scope should be stated explicitly in any Tier 3 report, not silently expanded.

pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.detail: generate_code_from_plan() embeds the full current contents of self_edit_generated.py plus CODE_OUTPUT_RULES ahead of the task text -- confirmed via direct source read. This is the intended manipulated variable for the Level-A test.
pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.who_generates_the_plan: the harness itself -- task['prompt'] (the frozen task text) is passed directly as the 'plan' argument; no separate plan-generation model call occurs, confirmed via source (generate_code_from_plan(plan: str, ...) takes plan as a literal string parameter, not something it derives via its own call)
pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.does_f1_alter_or_gate_the_candidate: no, confirmed observational-only in this harness (see M6)
pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.hidden_retries: none in this harness's own call path (self-edit's real intrinsic retry lives one level up, in execute_self_edit(), not invoked here)
pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.is_planning_framing_itself_architectural: prompt framing, by the definitions in the design doc's Level A/D distinction -- no decomposition into subtasks occurs; the current-file-context embedding is additional CONTEXT, squarely Level A, not Level D
pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.if_pipeline_wins: supports Level A (prompt/context framing helps) -- BUT ONLY once B1 (token budget) is fixed; as currently unfixed, a PIPELINE win could be fully explained by its 2x token budget alone, independent of framing
pipeline_vs_base1_analysis.if_pipeline_loses: supports a genuine Level-A null (framing doesn't help, at equal budget) -- but only informative once B1 is fixed; currently uninformative, since a loss even WITH 2x the token budget would be a strong null, while the current unfixed asymmetry makes a 'PIPELINE loses despite more tokens' result the more informative of the two possible unfixed-state outcomes, ironically

holdout_audit.evaluator_developed_using_these_tasks: no for the 8 new held-out tasks (they do not exist yet); yes for the underlying verify_in_sandbox()/clean_code() machinery, which was developed and debugged against the ORIGINAL 15-task suite's candidates -- a real, but already-disclosed and now cross-validated (22 real candidates, zero further extraction anomalies since the fix) risk, not a new one

statistical_audit.reasoning: paired binary outcomes on the same task across arms -- exactly McNemar's intended use case, and a real improvement over the prior pilot's unpaired two-proportion approach
statistical_audit.n8_meaningful: only for a large, pre-specified effect (25-30pp) -- correctly scoped as pilot-only, not confirmatory, in the design's own language
statistical_audit.effect_threshold_coherent: yes, consistent with this investigation's own prior power calculations for similarly-scaled binary/proportion endpoints
statistical_audit.multiplicity: present but minor (2 comparisons) -- see minor m1
statistical_audit.statistically_indistinguishable_used_inc: yes, as currently written -- see M5
statistical_audit.can_a_BASE_N_win_support_H4: yes, unambiguously -- if BASE_N (compute alone, no diversity) beats ARCH_COUNCIL, that is direct evidence AGAINST diversity/orchestration adding value, a clean H4-supporting (or even H2-supporting, if BOTH underperform in absolute terms) result
statistical_audit.can_failure_to_detect_H1_legitimately_su: only if the observed effect size is also small (see M5) -- a failure to detect at small n with a LARGE observed point estimate should NOT be read as H2 support, only as AMBIGUOUS
statistical_audit.can_design_distinguish_no_effect_from_un: not currently, without the M5 repair (point-estimate-plus-CI disambiguation rule)

infrastructure_audit.riverbrain_faiss_interaction_log_isolati: proven working empirically across 22 real candidates via the side_effects_so_far counter -- real, not assumed
infrastructure_audit.cross_arm_write_contamination: none observed or architecturally possible given the monkeypatch design, PROVIDED the same isolation layer is correctly reapplied to any new BASE_N code (not automatically inherited -- must be explicitly re-verified once BASE_N exists, per B2)
infrastructure_audit.condition_dependent_infrastructure_bias: plausible and NOT yet controlled -- see M4 (order randomization) and B1's own observation that swap/model-residency state accumulates across a session, which combined with fixed arm ordering could systematically favor or disfavor whichever arm runs first/last per task
infrastructure_audit.live_contention_confirmed: yes, directly observed (model_guided_autonomous_loop active during the prior pilot's own generation window) -- unresolved, will recur during Tier 3 unless run during genuinely lower-activity periods, which cannot be scheduled or guaranteed without authorization this audit does not have

evaluator_audit.can_evaluator_misclassify_an_architectur: yes, specifically via the still-unfixed truncation gap -- a PIPELINE or COUNCIL candidate that gets truncated (plausible, since neither currently has an explicit, correct token budget per B1) would read as a 'model logic failure' when the true cause is an infrastructure/budget artifact
evaluator_audit.spot_check_sufficiency: reasonable but not guaranteed to catch a single-arm-concentrated bias at pure-random 20% sampling (see minor m4)
evaluator_audit.evaluator_blind_to_condition: yes -- verify_in_sandbox() receives only code + test text, never a condition label, confirmed by source read

false_positive_pathways: B1 (token-budget asymmetry) left unfixed: ARCH_PIPELINE gets 2048 tokens vs BASE_1's 1024 default -- ARCH_PIPELINE could beat BASE_1 simply because it has twice the room to avoid truncation on a moderately long task, and this would be reported as 'Level A prompt framing works' when the true cause is 'more tokens works'. This is not a hypothetical risk -- it is the mechanically guaranteed default behavior of the current, unfixed code.

B3 (synthesis prompt reused verbatim) left unfixed: if BASE_N's synthesis call reuses SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_TEMPLATE's real 'council of perspectives'/'sharpest tension' framing on N attempts from ONE model, the model may manufacture or over-weight spurious disagreement among near-identical outputs, degrading BASE_N's own true ceiling -- making ARCH_COUNCIL look better than a fair, equally-capable same-model baseline would truly be, a false positive for H1 via baseline sabotage rather than genuine architectural merit.

M4 (order not randomized) left unfixed: if ARCH_COUNCIL happens to consistently run in a favorable cache/residency slot relative to BASE_N due to fixed ordering, an apparent COUNCIL advantage could be a real, measured effect of infrastructure state rather than the mechanism itself.
false_negative_pathways: Task-class mismatch: if the architecture's real value specifically lies in decomposition/multi-step/multi-file capability (the domain echo_projects and self-edit's own broader ambitions target), and Tier 3 tests only single-function, moderate-complexity tasks, a null result would correctly show 'no advantage on THIS task class' but could be misreported as 'architecture doesn't help', when the true, narrower finding is 'architecture doesn't help on tasks that don't need decomposition' -- a real, legitimate false-negative pathway distinct from any implementation bug.

If M2 (model pinning) is not fixed and the pinned model silently drifts between the development and held-out phases of the SAME study, a real architecture effect measured on the development set could fail to replicate on held-out data for a reason having nothing to do with generalization (Level G) -- a different model was actually being tested, not a failure of the mechanism to generalize.

If B3 is repaired by writing an OVERLY WEAK custom synthesis prompt for BASE_N (e.g., a bare 'pick the best one' with none of the real template's structured reasoning instructions), BASE_N could underperform its true ceiling for a reason unrelated to model diversity -- inflating an apparent ARCH_COUNCIL advantage into a false H1 positive via a different mechanism than B3's own first-listed risk (over-strong council framing) -- both directions of this specific repair carry real risk and neither should be assumed safe without checking the actual resulting BASE_N behavior on the development set first.

minimum_repairs_summary.repair: explicitly set max_tokens=2048 for every call in every arm
specify and build BASE_N's exact synthesis prompt, per-attempt temperature, and partial-failure handling before any code is written
minimally edit the real synthesis template's language + anonymize model labels, applied identically to BOTH BASE_N and ARCH_COUNCIL

pin the model once for the entire study via a persisted state file, not per-batch; separately confirm generate_code_from_plan()'s own internal choose_model() call is also intercepted/pinned for ARCH_PIPELINE specifically
add the unclosed-fence check to produce a real GENERATION_TRUNCATED classification
randomize arm order independently per held-out task
add a point-estimate + confidence-interval disambiguation rule to distinguish a genuine null from an underpowered one
relabel the F1 prediction as a structural fact confirmed by code inspection, not an experimental discovery

final_claim_boundary.what_tier3_can_establish_after_repairs: Whether council's real, combined mechanism (model diversity + real selection/ranking + real synthesis structure), at a token-and-call-count-matched budget, produces a detectably better or worse or indistinguishable pass rate than a single pinned model given the same total budget and a comparable (anonymized, equivalently-instructed) self-reconciliation step -- on 8 frozen, genuinely mechanism-untuned held-out coding tasks. Separately, whether self-edit's real prompt/context framing, at a token-matched single-call budget, helps, hurts, or does nothing relative to a bare task prompt, on the same held-out set.
final_claim_boundary.what_tier3_cannot_establish_even_after_r: Whether model diversity specifically (independent of council's structural/selection machinery) is the active ingredient in any observed council advantage (requires the DIVERSE_N arm, deliberately not added -- see M1). Whether any observed effect generalizes beyond single-function coding tasks to decomposition-heavy or multi-file domains (echo_projects' own territory). Whether the underlying models' capability ceiling would change under fine-tuning. Anything about learning, self-improvement, consciousness, or emergent capability in any sense beyond the specific, bounded, budget-matched comparison actually run.

recommended_next_action: Apply the three BLOCKER repairs (B1, B2, B3) and the four MAJOR repairs (M2-M6) to the design/prompt/token-budget SPECIFICATION before writing any BASE_N code. Then build and dry-run BASE_N against the 2 development tasks only, confirming its synthesis behavior is sane and its isolation layer is genuinely proven (not assumed inherited) before touching the held-out set.
